title: Boss: The Notebook
summary: Model a small notes app, save it, change it and query it, with nothing but a DbContext.

steps.title: The notebook
steps.body: A notes app needs one table and a handful of operations. You will build all of it: the entity, the context, and the methods the app calls. Each step builds on the one before, so keep your code: it is the whole program so far.

steps.title: The model
prompt: Write a `Note` entity and a `NotebookDb` context (`Data Source=notes.db`, a `DbSet<Note>` named `Notes`).
`Note` has: `int Id`, `string Title` (required), `string? Body` (optional), `bool Pinned`, and `int Words`, a column holding the number of words in the body.
Also give `Note` a read-only property `string Preview` (not a column): the first 10 characters of `Title`, or the whole title if it is shorter.
solution: public string Preview => Title.Length <= 10 ? Title : Title[..10];
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=notes.db");
template: Dojo.Check("Title is required", dojoSql.Contains("\"Title\" TEXT NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Body is optional", dojoSql.Contains("\"Body\" TEXT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Pinned and Words are columns", dojoSql.Contains("\"Pinned\" INTEGER NOT NULL") && dojoSql.Contains("\"Words\" INTEGER NOT NULL"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Preview is not a column", !dojoSql.Contains("Preview"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Eq("Preview of a long title", "Shopping l", new Note { Title = "Shopping list" }.Preview);
Dojo.Eq("Preview of a short title", "Ideas", new Note { Title = "Ideas" }.Preview);
Dojo.Eq("a note can be saved", 1, dojoDb.SaveChanges());

steps.title: Writing notes
prompt: Keep your model and add two methods at the **top** of your code (before the classes):

- `Note Write(NotebookDb db, string title, string? body)` creates a note, sets `Words` to the number of words in `body` (0 when it is null or blank; words are separated by spaces), saves it, and returns it.
- `bool Edit(NotebookDb db, int id, string body)` replaces a note's body, recomputes `Words`, and saves. Returns `false` when there is no such note.

template: Dojo.Eq("Write returns the saved note with its id", 1, dojoA.Id);
Dojo.Eq("Words counts words (extra spaces ignored)", 3, dojoA.Words);
Dojo.Eq("Words is 0 for no body", 0, dojoB.Words);
Dojo.Eq("Edit(1) returns true", true, Edit(dojoDb, 1, "just milk"));
Dojo.Eq("Edit saved the new body", "just milk", dojoNote.Body);
hints: A small helper `int CountWords(string? text)` keeps `Write` and `Edit` in step.

steps.title: Finding notes
prompt: - `List<string> Pinned(NotebookDb db)`: titles of pinned notes, alphabetical.
- `IQueryable<Note> Search(NotebookDb db, string word, int minWords)`: notes whose body contains `word` and that have at least `minWords` words, longest first (by `Words`, then by `Id`).
`Search` returns the query itself: the tests check its SQL to make sure the database does the work, so do not call `ToList` in it.
starter: IQueryable<Note> Search(NotebookDb db, string word, int minWords) => db.Notes;

protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=notes.db");
solution: IQueryable<Note> Search(NotebookDb db, string word, int minWords) =>
db.Notes.Where(n => n.Body != null && n.Body.Contains(word) && n.Words >= minWords)

template: Write(dojoDb, "Trip", "pack the tent and the stove");
foreach (var dojoN in dojoDb.Notes.Where(n => n.Title == "Shopping" || n.Title == "Diary")) dojoN.Pinned = true;
Dojo.Eq("Pinned is alphabetical", new List<string> { "Diary", "Shopping" }, Pinned(dojoDb));
Dojo.Check("Search filters in SQL", dojoSql.Contains("WHERE"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Check("Search sorts in SQL", dojoSql.Contains("ORDER BY"), dojoSql);
Dojo.Eq("Search(tent, 3) finds the longest first", new List<string> { "Trip", "Recipe" }, Search(dojoDb, "tent", 3).Select(n => n.Title).ToList());
Dojo.Eq("Search(tent, 1) includes the short note", new List<string> { "Trip", "Recipe", "Shopping" }, Search(dojoDb, "tent", 1).Select(n => n.Title).ToList());
